  1. Show HN: Take Voyager 1 apart, down to a single memory chip

    • Education
    • Space

    234 points · 57 comments · 18 Nov 2026, 16:18 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — An interactive Voyager project that lets visitors explore the two spacecraft and their story, from the mission scale down to a memory-chip/bit view. The landing page shows current distance and signal-time figures and links to journey and repair narratives.

    Discussion — The project drew enthusiasm for its presentation, but a technically knowledgeable commenter alleged modeling and factual inaccuracies. The author said the work used NASA/JPL material, acknowledged that RTG fuel spheres should be paired and that the Sun detector was not named, and supplied source links. A separate exchange covered the uncertain cause of Voyager 1's memory failure and cited NASA's statement that it cannot be determined with certainty.

  2. SpaceX catches the Starship to end Flight 15

    • Space

    1762 points · 1494 comments · 14 Nov 2026, 21:22 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — SpaceX’s Flight 15 page documented a Starship test flight that ended with a successful tower catch of the returning booster. The mission page presented the event as part of the company’s iterative flight-test program.

    Discussion — Commenters focused on the engineering spectacle and on the risks and operational value of catching a large booster at the launch tower. Discussion also covered launch cadence, whether the test objectives justified the approach, and comparisons with other reusable-launch systems.
